dengue.source: Ministry of Health figures as compiled by OpenDengue V1.3, Mendeley Data, the archived national open-data portal, and community-shared weekly files

monthly.national_label: Sum of the states that reported that month
monthly.note: Monthly state figures exist for ten states and end in December 2010 (OpenDengue).

yearly.note: 1999 to 2017 from Mendeley Data, 2018 to 2021 from the Ministry of Health's open data, 2023 from OpenDengue. For 2022 only Peninsular states are available, from a weekly district file whose source is not documented; Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan are blank that year. Kuala Lumpur includes Putrajaya.

weekly.note: Weekly state figures cover February 2010 to April 2015 and December 2019 to August 2022 for all states, continuing to December 2024 for Peninsular states. These files were shared online without a stated source or licence; we use them because their yearly sums agree with official totals. The gap from 2015 to 2019 is real: nothing weekly by state was found for those years. Kuala Lumpur includes Putrajaya.

weekly_models.skipped: too few cases to model (under 3 a week on average)

flu.source: WHO FluNet (national) and Ministry of Health statements (state clusters)
flu.note: No state-by-state influenza series is published in Malaysia, because influenza is not a notifiable disease. The only state figures are cluster counts in Ministry of Health statements during the 2025 surge: all states for weeks 43 to 45, and the five highest for week 40.
